chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
You proclaim the Takbeer on the night of Al-Fitr and the morning of Al-Fitr just as you proclaim the Takbeer during the Ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah).

key_terms.تُكَبِّرُ: You proclaim Takbeer (exalting God by saying 'Allahu Akbar')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and method for reciting Takbeer on the night of Eid al-Fitr?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal ruling for proclaiming the Takbeer during the night and morning of Eid al-Fitr, drawing a direct parallel to the practice during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. In Shia jurisprudence, this equivalence underscores the continuity of divine glorification from the conclusion of Ramadan's fasting to the commencement of the Eid celebration, reinforcing the ritual's status as a recommended act (mustahabb) that marks the transition from worship to gratitude. The narration highlights the communal and spiritual significance of vocalizing God's greatness as a public declaration of faith and joy upon completing the obligatory fast.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Exclaim Takbeer on the night of Al Fitr, and the morning of Al Fitr just as you did during the tenth (of Zilhajj)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
you should say Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) in the night and in the morning of al-Fitr just as you say it during the tenth (day of the month of Dhu al-Hajjah).”
